items.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DEVELOPING PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION COMPETENCE IN ESP
items.abstract: This thesis examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in developing professional communication competence among students studying English for Specific Purposes (ESP). It explores how AI-powered tools can support the development of speaking, writing, vocabulary, and interactional skills required in professional environments. Particular attention is paid to personalized learning, simulated professional communication, and immediate feedback. The thesis also considers the challenges associated with AI integration, including the reliability of generated information, overdependence on technology, and academic integrity. It argues that the effective use of AI, combined with teacher guidance and learner autonomy, can contribute to preparing students for professional communication in English.

items.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DOCUMENTING RELIGIOUS CULTURAL HERITAGE: A STUDY OF ITS POTENTIALS AND CHALLENGES
items.abstract: This study explores how artificial intelligence (AI) technologies can be employed to effectively enhance and document religious beliefs and practices. AI has the capability to process vast amounts of religious texts and sources, enabling the efficient extraction of significant information and patterns. Additionally, it facilitates the digitalization of religious heritage, ensuring its preservation for future generations. Smart applications also contribute to improving access to religious knowledge and fostering understanding between different cultures and religions. The use of AI in this field faces several challenges, including the need to consider the sensitivity of religious beliefs and rituals to avoid any negative reactions. Moreover, reliance on automated analysis may lead to the loss of cultural and spiritual context in traditional practices. Ensuring accuracy and avoiding bias is essential to preserving authentic values. Despite these challenges, AI offers promising opportunities for documenting religious heritage, provided that a balanced approach is adopted—one that acknowledges potential risks and respects the privacy and sanctity of religious beliefs.

items.title: The role of artificial intelligence in the modern Russian economy innovative development
items.abstract: Innovation is now not just one of the possible paths of development, but the main condition for the survival of any enterprise. The key factor that changes the paradigm of the innovation process is the ability to delegate routine operations. Previously, a significant portion of highly qualified employees’ time was spent on data collection and preliminary information processing, which considerably slowed down the research and development cycle. Modern technologies make it possible to completely delegate trivial tasks to intelligent systems, which are capable of processing such information much faster than a human. In today’s environment, the integration of autonomous intelligent systems is crucial for reducing operational costs. In 2026, artificial intelligence has transformed from an auxiliary technology into an indispensable tool for ensuring the competitiveness of knowledge intensive enterprises. The main areas of application of artificial intelligence have been analyzed, including the automation of business processes, generative design, and predictive analytics of production equipment. The main barriers that limit the implementation of automation systems based on artificial intelligence have been systematized and identified. It has been established that artificial intelligence has changed the methodology of research and development work, reducing the product development cycle from several months to several weeks. The conclusion is formulated that the integration of artificial intelligence tools into production processes reduces costs, the percentage of defective products, and requires staff to develop creative and strategic competencies. The role of artificial intelligence is defined not merely as an automation tool, but as an active participant in the innovation process, capable of creating innovative solutions. An author’s classification of barriers to the implementation of artificial intelligence in knowledge intensive industries has been developed.

items.title: The role of augmented reality in smart warehousing and supply chain optimisation
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of global supply chains (SC) under the Industry 4.0 (I4.0) paradigm has intensified the demand for efficiency, accuracy, and resilience in warehousing operations. Smart warehousing has emerged as a key driver of supply chain optimisation (SCO), integrating advanced digital tools to streamline inventory management, order fulfilment, and logistics coordination. Among these technologies, augmented reality (AR) has gained prominence due to its unique capability to enhance human performance by overlaying digital information onto the physical environment. Despite an increasing interest in related areas, there remains a lack of comprehensive understanding of how AR technologies are being integrated into SC initiatives under the I4.0 umbrella. To address this, the present study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of literature published between 2015 and 2025, using the “Web of Science” and “Scopus” databases as the primary sources. A total of 51 peer-reviewed articles were identified using a structured search query combining terms related to AR, I4.0, and SC optimisation. This work contributes by offering a comprehensive synthesis of the opportunities, challenges, and future directions of AR in smart warehousing. It provides actionable insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers seeking to leverage AR as a strategic tool for SC optimisation in the era of I4.0.

items.title: The Role of Digital Capabilities and Human Factors in Enhancing Port Service Performance: A Mediated Model for Eastern Indonesia
items.abstract: This research was conducted in response to the increasingly urgent need for digital transformation in port services in Eastern Indonesia to improve efficiency, transparency, and service quality amid the development of information technology. The research addresses a significant gap by integrating digital capabilities and human factors within the context of port digital transformation in Eastern Indonesia, an underexplored area in the existing literature. The research objective was to examine the influence of digital capabilities, human factors, and information system success on improvements in port service performance. The research method used a quantitative approach, with surveys of service users and system managers to measure technology acceptance and information system success. The number of respondents was 189. The use of a quantitative approach, including surveys and SEM-PLS analysis, is appropriate for testing complex relationships among variables. Based on the measurements, service performance (SP) obtained the highest score (R² = 0.732), supported by the organization's strong digital capabilities, effective human resources, and successful implementation of information systems. The anticipated outcomes include identifying critical factors that determine the success of digital transformation and developing an integrative model to guide the effective implementation of port services. The model linking digital capabilities, human factors, information system success, and port service performance provides a valuable framework for future empirical research.

items.title: The Role of Information Technology in Enhancing Customer Engagement in the Insurance Sector
items.abstract: The global insurance industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation, transitioning from rigid, product-centric operating models to agile, customer-centric ecosystems. Information Technology (IT) is the primary catalyst in this evolution, empowering insurers to connect with, understand, and serve their policyholders with unprecedented depth and precision. Traditional insurance models have long been characterized by impersonal interactions, fragmented data environments, slow response cycles, and a conspicuous absence of personalized service offerings—factors that collectively erode customer trust, engagement, and loyalty. This paper explores the multifaceted role of IT in enhancing customer engagement within the insurance sector, grounded in both academic literature and extensive practitioner experience across life, health, and annuity insurance domains. We propose a comprehensive conceptual framework that integrates diverse IT innovations—including Policy Administration Systems (PAS), unified customer data platforms, digital self-service portals, data analytics, artificial intelligence (AI), Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), cloud infrastructure, and omnichannel communication tools—to foster deeper, more meaningful, and enduring customer relationships. Our contribution is fourfold: first, we delineate a practitioner-informed conceptual framework for an IT-enabled customer engagement strategy in insurance, emphasizing omnichannel presence, data-driven personalization, and end-to-end policy lifecycle integration. Second, we examine the transformative potential of specific IT innovations, including AI-powered chatbots, predictive analytics engines, personalized digital portals, IoT-driven engagement, and cloud-hosted document management systems. Third, we contextualize these innovations through real-world implementation patterns observed across leading insurance carriers and reinsurers. Fourth, we discuss the strategic implications, implementation challenges, and actionable recommendations for insurers seeking to enhance customer loyalty, satisfaction, and long-term retention. By strategically leveraging IT and aligning technology investments with the customer journey, insurance companies can transcend transactional relationships and build enduring, value-driven connections with their policyholders—ultimately driving sustainable business growth and competitive advantage.

items.title: The Second Generation of AI / Второе поколение ИИ
items.abstract: An essay from The Bush Book. The smarter the model, the harder it is to spot an error in its text. A hybrid text is written by a human and a machine, creators of different natures who only seem to speak one language; it is fast, scalable, instrumental, and its errors may be contagious for people and for future models. The machine's answer is a "blank" that both work on, and both make mistakes; AI also carries people beyond their own competence, often under time pressure. The essay proposes a different basis for AI generations: not power or speed, but whether the human and the machine, working as one system, do no harm. The first generation extends a person; the second extends and protects, preventing errors before the signature reaches people. The image is the generations of fighter aircraft: the pilot must come home. Grows out of "The Snake's Tongue". A companion open specification sets out the idea in testable form. items.title: The Semiotics of AI-Generated Brand Narratives
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the symbolic architecture of brand storytelling, introducing new dynamics in how meaning is constructed, circulated, and interpreted. As tools like large language models and text-to-image generators become embedded in branding practices, they influence not only the production of content but the semiotic processes that define brand identity and consumer engagement. This chapter presents a conceptual framework for understanding AI-generated brand narratives as co-authored expressions shaped by algorithmic grammar, cultural codes, and audience interpretation. The framework emphasises the shift from human-centric storytelling to hybrid narrative systems, where machine-mediated outputs carry embedded signs, stylistic cues, and symbolic intent. It also addresses tensions around authenticity, emotional resonance, and brand coherence.The framework offers a theoretical lens for analysing how generative AI transforms brand meaning, positioning it as both a technological and cultural force in contemporary marketing communication.

items.title: The Speaker Under Surveillance
items.abstract: This chapter examines how language operates within the postdigital environment, where communication increasingly takes place through online platforms shaped by algorithms and data systems. It reconsiders language as a system of signs that is no longer stable, as the relationship between speaker and listener is constantly shifting under conditions of surveillance and digital mediation. The discussion introduces the idea of a “void in semiosis” to explain the growing gaps, ambiguities, and disruptions in meaning-making processes. It further argues that platforms collect behavioral data and reorganize communication into prestructured forms, influencing how individuals express thoughts and emotions. The chapter also reflects on how capitalist systems and artificial intelligence reshape linguistic practices by limiting spontaneity and embedding control within communication networks. In this changing environment, language becomes less personal and more regulated, raising concerns about the future of human expression, agency, and the diversity of linguistic experience.

items.title: The System Hallucination Scale (SHS): A Human-Centered Instrument for Assessing Perceived Reliability of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models routinely produce factually incorrect or misleading outputs, yet conventional automated benchmarks overlook how users perceive reliability during interaction. We introduce the System Hallucination Scale (SHS), a lightweight instrument modeling the famous System Usability Scale (SUS) and System Causability Scales (SCS). SHS measures perceived reliability across five dimensions: factual accuracy, source reliability, logical coherence, deceptiveness of presentation, and responsiveness to user guidance, using ten balanced Likert-scale items that provide a directional score and consistency diagnostic. In a supervised validation study with 193 participants (386 evaluations across 47 trained experimenters), SHS demonstrated strong internal consistency and high clarity, completing in an average of 4.2 minutes. Participants rated source verifiability and presentation deceptiveness worse than factual accuracy, indicating perceived vulnerabilities lie primarily in traceability and framing. As a proof of concept, SHS assesses human-perceived reliability rather than ground-truth correctness, providing open-source multilingual implementations and an interactive calculator.

items.title: The Window Is Not the Subject: Language Models, Context, and the Limits of a Consciousness Claim
items.abstract: Language models, context windows, and consciousness are now spoken of as if they formed a single object: a system that attends over a long window and is, in virtue of that attention, aware. This article states the connection the preceding notes and the empirical literature actually support, and the connection they rule out. At inference a language model is a conditional distribution over tokens given fixed parameters and a finite window. The window is the only channel by which a situation enters that computation. items.title: Through the looking glass: an empirical study of users’ experiences of the regulatory framework governing text and data mining and some practical ways forward
items.abstract: Text and data mining (TDM) refers to the process of uncovering knowledge from datasets using computational analysis. Applications of TDM have grown rapidly in recent years, especially with the ever-growing popularisation of Artificial Intelligence. TDM sheds light on knowledge hidden in the shadows, unlocking insights that drive discovery and innovation. TDM practices are governed by a complex patchwork of regulatory frameworks that encompasses several areas of law, not always specifically attuned towards regulating TDM, such as contract law, copyright and data protection and privacy regulatory frameworks. Doctrinal research in this context has been increasing in popularity in recent years, examining the legal frameworks, which collectively regulate TDM practices. However, socio-legal research in this regard is still emerging. This study, through 11 semi-structured interviews with users who have experience with conducting TDM, provides novel insights into users’ experiences with the regulatory frameworks that govern their practices. It offers valuable insights into the dynamics of TDM, including the strategies and motivations driving regulatory compliance. It also highlights how the current regulatory structure could be refined to create a more balanced approach; one that effectively regulates TDM while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders. Drawing on the study's findings, a set of recommendations are proposed, which aim to enable compliance with the existing regulatory framework for users, while still fostering both innovation and protection of stakeholder interests.

items.title: To airt – Proposal for an English Verb for Interacting with Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: “To airt” is proposed as an English verb for asking, prompting, consulting, or guiding an artificial intelligence in order to obtain information, ideas, advice, explanations, or other results. Example uses include: “Just airt it.”, “I already airted it.” and “Try airting it differently.” The proposal addresses an emerging lexical gap in everyday language. While “to google” provides a concise verb for searching the web, interaction with systems such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and other AI systems is commonly described using longer or provider-specific expressions. The proposed AI-related meaning of “to airt” has an additional semantic connection to the historical Scots verb “airt”, which is attested with meanings related to directing, guiding, or pointing the way. In prompting an AI, a user likewise gives direction to an artificial intelligence. The spelling also visibly begins with “AI”. This publication does not claim the word “airt” itself as a new coinage. It proposes and documents a new AI-related meaning and usage of the existing verb. The proposal was developed as an English counterpart to the German neologism “kinstlern”, proposed by the same author in August 2026 to mean “to ask or consult an AI”. The proposed usage is intended for general and unrestricted use.

items.title: ToFu: Exploiting and Fuzzing the LLM-Orchestrator-Tool Trust Boundary
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as agents that interact with external software through tools, with an orchestration layer translating model outputs into structured tool invocations. This architecture creates an LLM-orchestrator-tool trust boundary where tool semantics may go unenforced and LLM-generated arguments may be incorrectly treated as trusted. We present ToFu, a tool-aware framework that automatically derives semantic security checks for LLM tools from their existing metadata and a CWE-guided sanitizer corpus. ToFu specializes these checks to individual tools and automatically generates fuzzing harnesses and semantic oracles using runtime introspection and outcome sanitization. We evaluated ToFu across 273 MCP servers containing 3405 tools and identified verified bugs corresponding to CWE weakness classes in 343 tools across 118 of the servers. Our findings show that real-world tools frequently fail to enforce their documented input semantics, making it unsafe to treat LLM-generated arguments as trusted.

items.title: TopoLIA: Topology-Inspired Latent Interaction Attention for Drug Discovery
items.abstract: The growing sophistication of drug discovery calls for new advances in artificial intelligence (AI). Transformers have underpinned recent breakthroughs in AI, yet their conventional source-target attention mechanism can become a bottleneck for modeling complex interactions. Here, we introduce TopoLIA, a topology-inspired latent interaction attention mechanism that learns not only how much information should be exchanged between interaction partners, but also how that information should be transformed. Source-target-dependent attention is mediated through a compact latent interaction space, providing a structured representation of complex interactions. We further incorporate topological spectral representations to capture multiscale data geometry and extract algebraic relationships. TopoLIA thus incorporates topological principles into both data representation and neural network architecture. We demonstrate TopoLIA on protein-ligand binding, where persistent spectra encode multiscale topological and geometric patterns in 3D protein-ligand complexes, while latent interaction attention (LIA) enables structured, source-target-dependent information exchange. We pretrain TopoLIA by reconstructing masked multiscale spectral tokens from unlabeled molecular structures, yielding transferable structural representations without task-specific annotations. Across multiple scoring and docking benchmarks, TopoLIA achieves state-of-the-art performance and consistently outperforms its standard-attention counterpart. Rank analyses show that compact latent dimensions yield the best performance, supporting compact interaction spaces as an effective inductive bias for biomolecular learning. More broadly, LIA provides a general framework for structured, source-target-dependent information exchange that is applicable to diverse scientific and AI problems involving complex heterogeneous interactions.

items.title: Towards a Next Generation of Accounting Information Systems: A Systematic Literature Review Approach
items.abstract: Accounting Information Systems (AISs) are central to organisational decision-making, financial reporting, and regulatory compliance. Yet, the rapid digitalisation of financial operations has exposed these systems to cyber vulnerabilities, human errors, and inefficiencies in data management. To systematically examine these weaknesses, this paper employs a Systematic Literature Review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, analysing peer-reviewed journals, conference proceedings, and industry reports published between 2015 and 2025. The review identifies critical AIS vulnerabilities, including inadequate cyber controls, low human awareness of security risks, weak protection of digital assets, limited integration of risk management, absence of quantitative performance metrics, and restricted accessibility for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs). Based on these findings, a structured framework for next-generation AIS solutions is proposed, comprising real-time dashboards, cloud-based zero-trust architectures, hyper-automation, artificial intelligence-driven insights, blockchain, Internet of Things integration, self-healing systems, and adaptive risk engines. These interventions aim to strengthen data integrity, system resilience, regulatory compliance, and organisational agility, offering practical benefits to SMEs and large organisations operating in increasingly complex financial environments. Overall, the paper provides a comprehensive, evidence-based roadmap that bridges gaps in cybersecurity, operational efficiency, and decision-making within AIS, contributing valuable insights for practitioners, researchers, and policymakers seeking to modernise AISs while mitigating cyber, operational, and compliance risks.

items.title: Towards Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: A Review of Perturbation and Backpropagation-Based Methods
items.abstract: Machine and deep learning algorithms have been proven their efficiency in the medical domain. This is particularly noticeable in medical imaging, where these algorithms have demonstrated exceptional capabilities, often surpassing human experts in detecting diseases, segmenting anatomical structures, and in aiding diagnosis. However, despite their high performance, the non-transparency of these models has raised concerns about trust and explainability, especially in critical domains, such as healthcare. Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a promising field that, aims to make the decision-making processes of AI systems more interpretable and understandable to humans. By offering clear, human-understandable justifications, XAI enhances clinicians' trust in AI-assisted decisions, and supports the safe integration of these technologies into clinical workflows. This paper focuses on perturbation-based and backpropagation-based explainability methods that are widely adopted for convolutional neural networks in medical imaging. We intend to provide deeper insight into the relevance of XAI methods in medical imaging. We propose a structured taxonomy that categorizes these methods into perturbation and backpropagation-based approaches. For each category, we highlight their respective strengths, limitations, and areas of applicability. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges hindering the adoption of XAI and identify promising research directions to bridge the gap between high-performance AI models and their responsible deployment in real-world healthcare environments.

items.title: Training on the Standard, Judged by the Standard: The Benchmarking Paradox and Validation’s Impossibility in Human-LLM Co-Production
items.abstract: I built validation frameworks for Large Language Model (LLM) use in qualitative research and discovered that the more rigorously I validated, the more impossible validation became. This article theorises structural impossibility as the benchmarking paradox : LLMs train on human-generated text, then researchers validate outputs against human interpretation, which was the training source. Human interpretation functions simultaneously as training data, evaluation standard and outcome judged. Through diffractive reading of an empirical encounter where ChatGPT analysed policy texts, including vernacular translations it generated, I develop three theoretical coordinates: mimetic recursion (exposing circular validation), function/meaning incommensurability (revealing interpretation’s always-already hybrid nature) and epistemic authority redistribution (showing how computational infrastructure stratifies whose knowledge production counts). Empirically, GPT-5’s sophisticated meta-analysis of its own vernacular renderings exposes alignment priors determining computational legibility: whose voices register as analysable, which linguistic forms count as legitimate and what inquiries remain thinkable. The article argues that co-production through LLMs does not democratise qualitative research – it risks amplifying existing hierarchies while obscuring their operation through technical discourse. Rather than pursuing impossible validation, qualitative research should ask whose interpretive labour trained the pattern, contest whose interests human-LLM assemblages serve and demand that computational mediation generates epistemic and linguistic justice rather than reproducing the hierarchies it obscures.

items.title: Training User Simulators with Latent Intrinsic Feedback
items.abstract: User simulators are gaining attention as environments to train LLM assistants that can better cope with the nuances of multi-turn conversations with real users. Prior work on user simulation has emphasized generating realistic user utterances, leaving unexplored their potential as a source of direct feedback on the assistant's responses. Such evaluation signals may not be explicitly communicated in language, but can instead reside in the latent reasoning of users. In this work, we introduce user simulators with intrinsic feedback, namely, models equipped with latent evaluation states: internal thoughts, reactions, and scalar ratings that evaluate the assistant from a first-person user perspective at each conversation turn. We train LLM-based simulators using interaction logs between real users and assistants and demonstrate that intrinsic feedback improves simulation realism and critiquing behaviors versus prompted simulator baselines, while also providing turn-level evaluations that existing fine-tuned simulators lack. Further, evaluations generated by our trained simulators correlate better with human judgments than those of prompted simulators of the same size. Lastly, our experiments reveal that simulators with intrinsic feedback provide effective reward signals for multi-turn RL training, matching setups that rely on external judge LLMs for rewards while cutting RL compute by more than half.

items.title: Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a dominant paradigm for enhancing LLMs' reasoning capabilities. Yet long-horizon autoregressive rollouts introduce a fundamental limitation: local policy mismatch can compound into severe state distribution shift over trajectories. Existing LLM RL methods, such as GRPO and GSPO, control policy mismatch at the token or sequence level, but overlook this trajectory-induced shift, causing training instability and eventual collapse as the horizon grows. To close the state distribution gap, we propose Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO), a principled framework that theoretically derives the state-distribution correction from the off-policy policy gradient and incorporates it into the RL objective. TAPO further employs a geometric-mean estimator for variance reduction, together with a length-aware dynamic clipping that prevents overly deviated updates across the trajectory. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TAPO significantly surpasses existing LLM RL algorithms across eight competition-level benchmarks, achieving up to 48% and 12% improvement over GRPO on mathematical reasoning and algorithmic coding, with substantially enhanced training stability.

items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an important component of contemporary engineering education, offering opportunities to improve learning outcomes through data-driven instructional approaches.Technologies such as machine learning, intelligent tutoring systems, natural language processing, learning analytics, and generative AI facilitate personalised learning, automated evaluation, continuous progress tracking, and practical simulation-based experiences.This study presents the Artificial Intelligence-Driven Engineering Education Framework (AIEEF), developed to examine the impact of AI-enabled educational practices on student learning, engagement, and innovation.The framework was evaluated through a systematic review of existing research and empirical analysis of educational performance indicators.The results indicate notable improvements in student achievement, engagement, and participation in creative activities following the implementation of the proposed framework.Among the predictive models examined, Gradient Boosting achieved an accuracy of 94.2%, while overall student engagement increased from 68.7% to 89.8%.The study also considers challenges associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, algorithmic fairness, and academic integrity.The findings suggest that carefully designed AIsupported learning environments can enhance engineering education and assist institutions in preparing graduates for emerging technological and industrial requirements.

items.title: TRANSLATION OF PSYCHOLOGICAL AND EMOTIONAL LANGUAGE IN ELIF SHAFAK'S THE FORTY RULES OF LOVE: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF HUMAN AND AI TRANSLATION
items.abstract: The translation of psychological and emotional language presents a particular challenge because such language frequently depends on metaphor, cultural context, implicit meaning, interpersonal relationships, and the emotional positioning of the narrator. This article examines the translation of psychological and emotional expressions in Elif Shafak’s novel The Forty Rules of Love through a comparative analysis of human and artificial intelligence (AI) translation. The study focuses on how human translators and AI systems reproduce, modify, or omit emotionally and psychologically significant meanings. A qualitative comparative methodology is employed to examine selected examples representing such categories as love, grief, loneliness, spiritual transformation, inner conflict, desire, and emotional attachment. The analysis considers semantic accuracy, emotional intensity, metaphorical meaning, cultural appropriateness, stylistic naturalness, and preservation of the author’s literary voice. The findings suggest that AI translation can provide relatively accurate lexical and syntactic renderings of explicit emotional statements, while human translation demonstrates greater sensitivity to contextual ambiguity, metaphor, cultural references, and subtle psychological states.

items.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop a data-driven predictive framework to assess and forecast respiratory morbidity risks associated with air pollution and climate variability across the UAE, addressing the gap in region-specific health-environment models. Design/Methodology/Approach: Using environmental data from the National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) and health data from the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP), machine learning models, namely Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), will be applied to analyse time-series data integrating air pollutants, namely Particulate Matter ≤ 2.5 μm (PM₂.₅), Particulate Matter ≤ 10 μm (PM₁₀), Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂), Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂), Ozone (O₃), Carbon Monoxide (CO), together with meteorological factors (temperature, humidity, wind speed). Findings: The expected outcome is an explainable AI system capable of issuing early warnings for high-risk respiratory health days, improving predictive accuracy through multi-factor integration. Original/Value of the Paper: The study contributes an innovative, UAE-specific, explainable AI framework that supports public health resilience, hospital preparedness, and environmental policy under UAE Vision 2031. items.title: Truth, Doubt, and Persuasion in Liquid Digital Environments: Toward a Liquid Epistemology of Algorithmic Mediation, Epistemic Communities, and Generative AI (2006–2026)
items.abstract: This study examines how truth claims are constructed, contested, and negotiated within the liquid digital environment, extending Zygmunt Bauman's (2000, 2007) theory of liquid modernity into digital epistemology. Using a triangulated qualitative design combining phenomenological inquiry, digital ethnography, and critical discourse analysis, the research investigated how individuals navigate competing truth claims within an increasingly fluid and algorithmically mediated information ecosystem. Data comprised 45 in-depth interviews with social media users in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada; 12 months of digital ethnographic observation across six platforms; and critical discourse analysis of 500 digital interactions concerning contested truth claims posted between 2016 and 2025. The findings show that the digital environment has reorganized the epistemic frameworks through which participants assess reality, producing adaptive credibility strategies alongside heightened ontological insecurity. Three mechanisms emerged through which digital liquidity shapes truth perception: algorithmic mediation of visibility, performative authenticity across multiple identities, and epistemic communities that sustain parallel truth ecosystems. Seventy-eight percent of participants reported diminished confidence in discerning truth online, even as they described sophisticated heuristics for managing uncertainty, including lateral reading, epistemic patience, and the cultivation of algorithmic personas. Awareness of generative artificial intelligence produced a condition of synthetic doubt, in which the mere possibility of machine authorship became grounds for doubting any content. Integrating these findings with recent experimental, meta-analytic, and philosophical scholarship on algorithmic amplification, testimonial trust, and synthetic media, the study proposes liquid epistemology as a framework capturing the fluid, contextual, and perpetually renegotiated character of truth in digital spaces, considers its transferability to high-connectivity, high-trust societies such as Saudi Arabia, and identifies priorities for comparative, longitudinal, and intervention research.

items.title: Turkish yoga consumers’ motivation: A scale development study
items.abstract: In the growing yoga market, the purchasing behavior of yoga consumers constitutes one of the important research areas. Turkey is a new market for yoga. Information on the reasons and motivations of consumers in this market for purchase of yoga-related services/products is quite limited. For this reason, this study aims to develop a valid and reliable scale to determine the motivations of yoga consumers in Turkey to participate in yoga. The study was structured based on the Scale Development Process. A three-stage process consisting of Item Development, Scale Development and Scale Evaluation was carried out. As a result of the study, a scale consisting of 5 dimensions and 24 items was obtained. The scale shows that yoga consumers in Turkey have intrinsic motivations related to escape and achievement and extrinsic motivations related to visibility, socialization and reference. We hope that the scale developed in this study will contribute to the field in terms of identifying and making sense of the motivations of yoga consumers in similar markets such as Turkey, where yoga is/will be newly developing.

items.title: Tutorial: Extracting Unstructured Text Using Large Language Models
items.abstract: This tutorial shows how to build a two-stage pipeline in which a multimodal large language model reads each page as an image and a second model turns the extracted text into structured JSON. items.title: Ubuntu, African Ethics, and Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence in Project Management: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is progressively revolutionising project management by enhancing forecasting, planning, decision-making, risk evaluation, and organisational efficacy. Nevertheless, escalating apprehensions about trust, accountability, equity, transparency, and human supervision have underscored the necessity for governance strategies that transcend mere technical efficacy. This research performs a concept-focused systematic literature review to investigate the convergence of Ubuntu, African ethics, Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence (HCAI), and project governance. This research consolidates disparate knowledge domains related to responsible AI, HCAI, ethical leadership, stakeholder governance, organisational preparedness, and Ubuntu-informed leadership, stakeholder inclusivity, and a comprehensive Ubuntu-informed human-AI governance framework, utilising peer-reviewed literature from 2022 to 2026. This research posits that Ubuntu offers a unique governance viewpoint rooted in collective responsibility, relational leadership, and human dignity. The results indicate that Ubuntu-informed AI governance can assist African governments and policymakers in establishing ethical and responsible frameworks. This research establishes a basis for subsequent investigations on Ubuntu, artificial intelligence governance, and project management. The results underscore the significance of ethical leadership, stakeholder engagement, human supervision, and responsibility for project management professionals in responsible AI-driven project settings.

items.title: Understanding AI Use at Work: Trust, User Experience, and Basic Psychological Needs in U.S. and Chinese Workers
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in the workplace, yet less is known about how workers experience AI and whether these experiences differ across countries. The present work compared workplace AI use and attitudes in 225 workers in China and 198 workers in the United States. Participants completed measures describing their work practices, attitudes and motivation toward AI (GAAIS; Schepman & Rodway, 2020, 2023; TENS-Life; Peters et al., 2018; Schrepp et al., 2017; Jian et al., 2000). Using Self-Determination Theory, we also examined whether autonomy, competence, and relatedness were associated with weekly AI use through trust and mistrust in AI. Chinese workers reported using AI more hours per week and reported greater organizational support for AI use than U.S. workers. They also reported more positive and more negative attitudes toward AI, as well as greater mistrust. Chinese workers reported lower AI-supported autonomy and competence but greater AI relatedness than U.S. workers. Mediation analyses indicated that relatedness was indirectly associated with greater weekly AI use through greater trust in AI in both samples. The findings suggest that understanding workplace AI use requires attention not only to the technology itself, but also to workers’ psychological and social experiences with AI.

items.title: Understanding ChatGPT adoption among medical students: an integrated theoretical model of psychological barriers and individual factors
items.abstract: Background The growing adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly ChatGPT, has created new opportunities for medical education by supporting learning, problem-solving, and knowledge acquisition. However, evidence regarding the psychological and individual factors influencing ChatGPT adoption among medical students remains limited. This study develops and tests an integrated theoretical model that combines Privacy Theory, Technostress Theory, Affect Theory, Diffusion of Innovation Theory, and the Theory of Planned Behavior to explain ChatGPT adoption. Material and methods A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate medical students at King Faisal University, Saudi Arabia using a structured, self-administered questionnaire. The proposed model examined the effects of privacy concern, technophobia, guilt feelings, and innovativeness on behavioral intention and ChatGPT usage behavior, with behavioral intention serving as the mediating variable. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results The findings showed that innovativeness had a significant positive relationship with behavioral intention ( β = 0.579, p < 0.001), while behavioral intention had a strong positive relationship with ChatGPT usage behavior ( β = 0.777, p < 0.001). In addition, behavioral intention significantly mediated the relationship between innovativeness and ChatGPT usage behavior ( β = 0.450, p < 0.001). In contrast, privacy concern, technophobia, and guilt feelings were not significantly related to behavioral intention, and their indirect relationships with ChatGPT usage behavior were also not significant. Conclusion Within the proposed model, personal innovativeness was the only antecedent significantly associated with behavioral intention, whereas the psychological barriers were not statistically significant. By integrating five complementary theoretical perspectives into a single framework, this study extends current understanding of generative AI adoption in medical education and highlights behavioral intention as the key mechanism linking individual characteristics to actual use. The findings provide theoretical insights and practical guidance for promoting the responsible and effective integration of ChatGPT into medical education through initiatives that foster innovativeness and AI literacy.

items.title: Understanding Social Bias in Multimodal Learning Systems: A Taxonomy and Framework
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of multimodal learning systems across high-stakes applications has intensified concerns about fairness and social bias, yet existing research remains scattered across modalities, tasks, protected attributes, mitigation strategies, and evaluation methodologies. This survey provides an overview of fairness and social bias in multimodal artificial intelligence. By reviewing 44 papers and 16 datasets, we synthesize the current landscape of fairness research in multimodal systems and identify emerging challenges and research opportunities. Our primary contribution is twofold. First, we introduce a multi-dimensional taxonomy that organizes the literature across nine operational dimensions, providing a unified perspective on multimodal fairness research. Second, we propose an end-to-end operational lifecycle framework that illustrates how biases emerge within shared latent spaces and identifies targeted pre-processing, training-time, and post-training intervention strategies. Overall, this survey discusses key performance-fairness trade-offs and provides a structured roadmap for evaluating and mitigating bias, ultimately supporting the development of more equitable multimodal AI systems.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been a silent presence in research for several years, and through various technologies, AI has become ever-present in qualitative studies. As AI continues to proliferate and its use expands both outside and within scholarship, the use of AI in research has evolved from a resource for qualitative scholars to a tool for study participants to use as they engage with our research studies. We had separate encounters with research participants using AI to author narratives in our dissertation studies. Through examples from our studies, this article explores the impact of AI use by study participants.

items.title: Unregulated Allies: A Mixed-Methods Systematic Review of Large Language Model Integration, Implementation Outcomes, and Policy Frameworks in University Mental Health
items.abstract: This mixed-methods systematic review examines the evidence for the safe integration of large language model (LLM)-based mental health support into university counseling services, and the policy, ethical, and governance frameworks that shape that integration. The review is guided by a convergent segregated design (Hong et al., 2018) and reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 (Page et al., 2021) and ENTREQ (Tong et al., 2012). Four theoretical perspectives structure the review: the RE-AIM framework for implementation science (Glasgow et al., 1999), biomedical ethics (Beauchamp & Childress, 2019), AI governance (Floridi et al., 2018; Novelli et al., 2024), and an integrated model of LLM-mediated mental health support, with cultural responsiveness as a cross-cutting dimension. A four-block Boolean search was executed across EBSCOhost, ProQuest, PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and IEEE Xplore (plus Cochrane CENTRAL), yielding 2,172 records; after filtering, 365 topic-relevant records were screened, 151 unique records were identified, and 138 full texts were retrieved for deep text screening. Data are extracted across twelve domains covering study and intervention characteristics, quantitative and safety outcomes, therapeutic alliance, RE-AIM implementation dimensions, policy and governance, qualitative findings, MMAT 2018 quality appraisal, and meta-analysis data. A random-effects meta-analysis was pre-specified for any outcome domain with at least three comparable studies; following data extraction, this was not feasible because fewer than three studies per outcome domain reported between-group effect sizes in a common metric, means and standard deviations were frequently unreported, and pre-post correlations were not reported in any study. Quantitative synthesis therefore proceeds as a structured narrative synthesis (Popay et al., 2006; McKenzie & Brennan, 2021) with direction-of-effect coding, thematic synthesis of qualitative findings using a 40-theme framework, and a narrative policy and governance synthesis, integrated at the interpretation stage across the RE-AIM dimensions. GRADE is applied at the outcome level using a structured narrative approach (Murad et al., 2017).

items.title: User Preferences for Enhanced Robot Adaptation in Assistive Tasks
items.abstract: The adaptation of robot behaviour to each user can be seen as an ergonomic feature. Adaptation plays a key role in increasing human–robot interaction efficiency and safety, and this is especially relevant in assistive scenarios, where users may be unable to adapt to the robot or help in task execution. Robot adaptation may happen at different levels of abstraction, from low-level trajectory parameters to higher-level task concepts. These higher-level abstractions relate to human factors such as personal preferences on how the robot should perform the task. This chapter introduces the concept of user preferences to adapt the robot’s behaviour and also help in the robot’s decision-making, with a special focus on assistive robotic tasks such as dressing or feeding a user with mobility impairments. It also presents the challenges associated with adaptation in this kind of scenario, as well as some existing methods that may be used to adapt robot behaviour to high-level abstract preferences. Such adaptation makes it easier for the user to interact with the robot in a more efficient and comfortable manner, thus improving its ergonomics.

items.title: User-Centred Ecological Interface Design (UCEID)
items.abstract: User-Centred Ecological Interface Design (UCEID) is a human factors framework designed to be used in the early stages of interface design. This suite of methods was used to determine what features Mobility as a Service (MaaS) required to not only be a genuinely useful and effective journey planning tool but also accessible to all ages and genders to ensure travel equity. Methods used included benchmarking MaaS apps, holding focus groups looking at in-app iconography, and Design with Intent workshops leading to design concepts and storyboards. As a result, design recommendations were provided to optimise the initial product design.

items.title: Validation of a computer-vision milking parlour monitoring system
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can help identify suboptimal milking practices and provide reports without time-consuming visits. The objective of this study was to validate a computer-vision milking parlour monitoring system (CVS, Cattle Care Inc.) by comparing its reports against trained human observers (n = 2, comparison method). A camera was installed in the parlour of two dairy farms in Ontario, Canada, one operating a herringbone parlour and the other a parallel parlour. Four one-hour segments (2 per farm), selected by the CVS, were independently analysed by human observers and the CVS. Prep-lag time, average unit-on time, turn time, and milking protocol deviations were assessed in each shift and compared between methods. For continuous variables, Lin’s concordance correlation coefficients (CCC) were calculated to evaluate the agreement between CVS and human observers; Bland–Altman plots were used to assess systematic bias. For categorical variables, the F-score was calculated to assess event-detection performance. The CCC for unit-on time (n=44 milking turns) was 0.999 (95% CI: 0.999-0.999), for prep-lag time (n = 214 cows) was 0.995 (95% CI: 0.994–0.996) and for turn time (n = 25 turns) was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.997–0.999). All protocol deviations flagged by the human observers (n = 51 events) were detected by the CVS; six towel misuse events detected by the CVS were missed by the human observers. An F-score of 1 was obtained for the CVS method. Under the conditions tested, the CVS demonstrated high agreement with human observations for prep-lag time, unit-on time, turn time, and milking-protocol deviations, while also identifying some events not detected by human observers. The assessed technology may complement human expertise by enabling more efficient and streamlined assessment of milking parlour performance.

items.title: Vibe Coding: An experiment with test-driven development
items.abstract: Abstract Context Conversational Large Language Models (CLLMs) can automatically generate code by collaborating with users through natural language. However, poor collaboration can lead to poor quality output. Objective This exploratory study aims to investigate how humans and CLLMs can collaborate as peers through vibe coding, an approach that integrates principles from prompt engineering, agile design, and human-AI co-creation to enhance collaboration. Method We designed four interaction models representing different collaboration patterns in the software development process: the solo model (human-only development), the collaborative model (human–CLLM collaboration), the fully automated model (development autonomously performed by a CLLM), and the agentic model (development autonomously performed by the MetaGPT X platform). Based on these models, we implemented corresponding Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflows using structured prompts and Python scripts. We then conducted a controlled pre-experimental study with TDD professionals to compare the solo and collaborative workflows. In addition, we performed repeated exploratory executions of fully automated and agentic workflows on the same development tasks to obtain complementary evidence. Results Our findings suggest that the choice of interaction model should depend on the development objective. Agentic workflows are best suited for rapid development and functionally correct production code but may introduce additional implementation complexity. However, they may also introduce additional implementation decisions that are not explicitly required by the functional specifications, resulting in untested decision points. In contrast, collaborative workflows produce higher-quality, better-organized test suites. Conclusions Our work explored how humans can collaborate with CLLMs in generating code in highly intensive and demanding development process. Our results also show that accurately reproducing development process workflows is yet an open problem, also in the new agentic technologies.

items.title: Virtualism: A Reserve-Based Income and Monetary Framework for the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is weakening the link between production and labor income on which capitalist economies distribute purchasing power. This paper argues that redistribution financed by taxation or public debt, including conventional universal basic income (UBI), cannot close this gap at scale, and proposes an alternative framework, Virtualism. Each person is endowed with a basic reserve equal to their remaining years up to an agreed lifespan (80 years), measured in hours (Time-Money), valued against a decent-living standard and released monthly to the family account on the condition of basic work: community service in one's own village. The reserve is allocated across four accounts (household 70%, enterprise 20%, village fund 5%, basic tax 5%), is non-inheritable and extinguished at death, while gains from its management are inheritable. Money is issued against this human reserve rather than through interest-bearing debt; existing wealth and prices are preserved through a one-time fixed conversion, after which exchange rates float. A collective per-capita production cap and a virtue rating that prices ethical conduct complete the framework. Illustrative calculations for Indonesia suggest that a debt-financed UBI at a decent-living standard would exceed ten times state revenue, whereas the proposed system requires no budgetary outlay and yields basic tax revenue of about IDR 1,680 trillion a year. The binding constraint shifts from finance to real production. The same formula applies in any currency: a United States illustration yields identical hours of life at a different money value, and a working web prototype demonstrates the mechanism. The paper discusses trade-offs, open questions, and a proposed one-year pilot in five villages on Adonara, Flores (1,250 people, about USD 8 million).

items.title: Vocal Loudness and Stability as Behavioral Indicators of Surgeons’ Non-Technical Skills
items.abstract: Non-technical skills (NTS) are essential for safe surgical teamwork, while objective measures of how surgeons communicate remain limited. This pilot study examined whether sentence-level vocal loudness and stability distinguish simulated good- and bad-NTS conditions and identified the voice features most sensitive to NTS differences. Three surgical education fellows completed three scenarios under both conditions. Good- and bad-NTS events were designed to reflect NOTSS scores of 4 and 1. Surgeon speech was isolated, vocal intensity was quantified using root-mean-square (RMS) amplitude, and sentences were classified as low, normal, or high volume relative to event-specific reference levels. Vocal stability was assessed using state entropy and state-persistence probability. Bad-NTS events showed greater loudness, more frequent extreme-volume states, higher entropy, and lower persistence, with moderate-to-large effects (|δ| ≥ .60). Mean event-level RMS, high-volume-state frequency, state entropy, and state persistence were the most sensitive features (|δ| > .80), supporting their use in objective NTS assessment.

items.abstract: Technische Normen sind eine zentrale Grundlage beruflicher Arbeit im Bauwesen. Generative KI-Systeme verändern den Zugang zu ihnen und den Aufbau normativen Fachwissens. Der Beitrag analysiert Potenziale und Grenzen KI-gestützter Anwendungen zur Erschließung von Normeninhalten für das berufliche Arbeiten und Lernen. Zugleich wird gezeigt, dass KI-generierte Antworten kritisch auf fachliche Richtigkeit und Normenkonformität geprüft werden müssen. Daraus ergeben sich neue Anforderungen für die berufliche Bildung im Bauwesen. Technical standards constitute a fundamental basis for professional practice in the construction industry. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems are transforming access to these standards and the development of normative professional knowledge. This paper examines the potential and limitations of AI-supported applications for facilitating access to the content of technical standards in vocational work and learning. It also demonstrates that AI-generated responses must be critically evaluated with regard to their technical accuracy and compliance with applicable standards. These developments give rise to new requirements for vocational education and training in the construction sector.

Our digital photos, global banking transactions, medical research, and artificial intelligence models are all preserved inside massive data centers on physical magnetic tapes and optical media. However, due to the fundamental laws of physics, these physical materials inevitably degrade, fade, and accumulate microscopic scratches over decades. When a playback drive attempts to read this worn surface, severe data corruption occurs, leading to permanent information loss. While global technology conglomerates attempt to solve this lifespan crisis by developing expensive, exotic new materials in laboratories, the VTAS-Hybrid architecture developed by Tommi von Aronen introduces a complete revolution: it accepts material imperfection and rescues the data using software intelligence. 🧠 How VTAS-Hybrid Works (In Plain English) VTAS-Hybrid acts as an "intelligent brain" installed directly into the readout drive. items.title: Vulnerable Models in the AI Supply Chain: An Empirical Study of Adoption, Propagation, and Usage Patterns
items.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models has established a complex supply chain, but many of these shared artifacts harbor severe vulnerabilities such as insecure serialization and architectural backdoors. While prior efforts have extensively scanned model registries to flag malicious artifacts, a critical gap remains in understanding how developers actually adopt and integrate these unsafe models into downstream software systems. We bridge this gap by conducting a large-scale empirical study on the usage and propagation of 16,977 known vulnerable models on HuggingFace flagged by InsightDB. We track their prevalence across GitHub repositories, software packages, fine-tuning chains, and deployed applications. Our analysis reveals that, despite being publicly flagged, these vulnerable models appear in over 21,000 code locations across more than 5,000 open-source repositories, with 3,757 distinct flagged models (22.1\%) actively referenced in at least one project. To understand how these models are integrated in code and identify recurring usage patterns, we categorize and analyze the recurring patterns surrounding them via a customized pipeline that combines Code Property Graphs extraction with a tailored Frequent Subgraph Mining approach. Across all patterns, we find no evidence of provenance verification or model sanitization logic, with developers frequently bypassing security parameters or delegating trust to permissive framework defaults. These findings underscore that scanning model files alone is insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for context-aware security analysis and stricter integration guardrails at the application layer of the AI supply chain.

items.title: Warehouse logistics and task switching theory revisited: asymmetric height switching costs in order picking systems
items.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the impact of pick location height switching on task performance time in manual order picking systems. Drawing on task switching theory, we examine whether switching between ground- and chest-level pick locations increases task performance time, whether switching costs are asymmetric, and whether item weight strengthens possible differences between ground-to-chest and chest-to-ground switches. Design/methodology/approach We adopt a two-stage approach that combines internal validity and operational generalizability. First, a controlled eye-tracking experiment simulates a simplified order picking scenario to explore the cognitive mechanisms underlying visual search when repeating versus switching pick location heights. Second, we analyze 3,537,973 pick location visits from a German grocery retail warehouse to test the effects of pick location height switching in a real-world operational environment with professional order pickers. Findings The eye-tracking experiment provides mechanism-oriented evidence that switching between pick location heights increases visual search time and reorientation demands under controlled conditions. The archival field study complements these behavioral insights by showing that height switching is associated with longer task performance time. It further shows that switching costs depend on direction, with ground-to-chest switches being more time-consuming than chest-to ground switches. This directional difference becomes more pronounced as item weight increases. Practical implications The findings suggest that warehouse managers should consider not only the frequency but also the direction of height switches when designing picking sequences. Batching and routing algorithms could incorporate switching costs as a weighted parameter, with particular attention to ground-to-chest switches involving heavier items. However, reducing height switches should be balanced against ergonomic risks, as long sequences of ground-level picks may increase repetitive bending and musculoskeletal strain. Originality/value This study provides the first empirical evidence on pick location height switching in warehouse operations and extends task switching theory to a new operational context. By combining mechanism-oriented eye-tracking evidence with large-scale field data, we show that height switching is associated with asymmetric switching costs and provide insights into the cognitive and motor reorientation processes that may underlie these effects.

items.title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming direct users of the open web. As they take on increasingly complex and information-intensive tasks, effective web access is becoming a core capability for agentic problem solving. Existing approaches have advanced agentic web access through different access models, including search-augmented agents, browser-based agents, and, more recently, filesystem-based agents. Nevertheless, as users expect agents to complete long-horizon, end-to-end tasks, they increasingly need to conduct broad information gathering, perform browser actions, and revisit acquired evidence within a single trajectory. Yet our preliminary analyses reveal that existing access models struggle to meet these demands. They primarily support either information gathering or browser interaction, while combining their capabilities can involve substantial costs or performance trade-offs. To this end, we present Web\$hell, an interface that unifies web access under a single access model. Using a common schema defined by WebContract, WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects. These objects are maintained in WebCache and handled through a shared set of operations, providing agents with consistent, operable, and persistent web access. Through extensive experiments across web search, web navigation, and deep research benchmarks, we show that Web\$hell achieves strong task performance at lower cost. Our results further indicate the importance of interface design for effective web access, with Web\$hell opening new possibilities for more capable and efficient LLM agents on the web.

items.title: What “Digitization” Means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port (Cameroon) Project: Definitions, Components, Pathways, and Implications
items.abstract: Digitization in the deep sea port context is often invoked as shorthand for technological modernization, yet its operational meaning and implications vary widely by place. This paper explicates what “digitization” means for the Limbe Deep Sea Port in Cameroon by situating the concept within port operational processes, stakeholder relationships, governance environments, and socioeconomic constraints specific to Limbe and comparable West/Central African ports. Drawing on an interdisciplinary desk-based literature review of academic studies, international agency reports, industry white papers, and regional policy documents, the study adopts a conceptual-analytical approach to define digitization as the systematic conversion and integration of analogue and paper-based port procedures into interoperable digital systems that enable real-time data exchange, automated workflows, evidence-based decision-making, and secure electronic transactions across the port ecosystem. The paper disaggregates digitization into technological (TOS, PCS, VTMS, IoT, analytics, blockchain, cybersecurity), organizational (process re-engineering, governance, procurement), human factors (skills, roles, change management), and regulatory (single window, data governance) dimensions. It identifies measurable indicators to assess progress—transaction digitalization rate, vessel turnaround time, dwell time, customs clearance time, system uptime, and workforce certification rates—and outlines likely benefits (efficiency, transparency, environmental monitoring, regional connectivity) and risks (digital divides, cyber threats, governance bottlenecks, finance constraints). The analysis highlights contextual enablers and barriers for Limbe, including infrastructure, institutional capacity, financing options, and regional integration imperatives. The paper concludes with policy and operational recommendations that prioritize staged interventions—low‑complexity quick wins, mid‑term integration, and long‑term smart-port capabilities—anchored in inclusive governance, blended finance, workforce development, and cyber resilience. The findings aim to provide a clear, practical, and academically grounded definition of digitization tailored to Limbe’s developmental and geopolitical realities. Keywords: Limbe Deep Sea Port; port digitization; Port Community System; Terminal Operating System; Cameroon; smart ports; maritime governance

items.title: What If AI Agents Had to Prove What Actually Happened Before Being Allowed to Continue?
items.abstract: An AI agent may be authorized to act—but what happens when the real-world result differs from what was authorized? Should that agent still be allowed to continue? As frontier AI models evolve into autonomous systems capable of executing payments, transmitting sensitive information, modifying infrastructure, invoking privileged tools, and controlling physical devices, a fundamental security question emerges: Why should authorization granted before an action remain sufficient when its actual consequences have not yet been independently verified? This paper proposes a different model of machine authority: “Computation is not authority to act. Authority must be earned from the real execution path, not granted indefinitely per session.” The research introduces Receipt-Gated Interim Effectuation Validation (IEV), an execution-control architecture in which a consequential operation may first produce a real but strictly bounded effect. Protected evidence of what actually occurred is subsequently examined by an independent validator. Only successful validation establishes the protected continuation condition required for a subsequent, potentially broader effect. The distinction is fundamental: the AI agent's assertion that an action succeeded is not proof that it happened correctly, and a receipt alone is not authorization to continue. The proposed architecture incorporates: Real-effect validation: Verification of actual outcomes rather than reliance solely on predicted behavior, proposed commands, or self-reported success. Receipt-gated continuation: Subsequent effectuation depends on protected validation of the preceding bounded effect. Independent execution authority: Separation of the AI computation environment from protected policy, credential, validation, and effectuation components. Software–hardware enforcement: Continuation conditions realized through cryptographic objects, derived or split keys, protected state, hardware latches, or equivalent mechanisms. Finality Sink verification: Independent checks at the effect-capable boundary, including act, destination, scope, phase, freshness, and revocation conditions. Taint and provenance controls: Consideration of untrusted inputs, prompt-injection exposure, credential surrogation, and privilege-separated execution. Fail-closed recovery: Explicit handling of missing receipts, uncertain outcomes, conflicting authentic evidence, validator compromise, crash recovery, and unauthorized retries. Controlled escalation: Protected human review, bounded automated remediation, reduced-scope continuation, and termination where required. The paper develops a formal protocol vocabulary, validation predicates, continuation mechanisms, six conformance profiles, implementation-invariance rules, illustrative workflows, and an analytical model of residual exposure. Potential applications include frontier AI agent infrastructure, autonomous tool execution, cloud and network operations, financial transactions, critical infrastructure, and robotic systems. The central research proposition is that AI safety should not end at the moment permission is granted. For consequential autonomous operations, the authority to proceed can be made technically dependent on independently verified evidence of what actually occurred. This publication presents a proposed architecture and analytical design, not an experimentally validated production system. It does not establish that any existing commercial platform implements the proposed mechanisms. Patent disclosure: The architecture described in this publication is identified as patent pending under Indian Patent Office application 202631117633, titled “Systems and Methods for Cryptographically Staged Effectuation with Verified Partial Effect, Receipt-Bound Full Effectuation, and Software-Hardware Enforcement.” Patentability, enforceable scope, and relationships to other technologies are not determined by this publication. Independent technical review, adversarial evaluation, implementation criticism, and discussion of related prior art are welcomed.

items.title: What Is the Best Word to Describe AI Uncertainty: Confidence, Certainty, Reliability, or Accuracy?
items.abstract: AI systems are increasingly common in decision-making tasks. However, these systems often generate probabilistic responses, resulting in uncertainty in their outputs. Understanding this uncertainty can help users make robust decisions, such as when to trust the agent and whether to seek more information. Interpreting uncertainty is not always straightforward, though; past work shows there is variability in how people interpret probabilistic information (e.g., weather forecasts). This study builds on that research by analyzing how people interpret probabilistic AI responses. In this survey-based experiment ( N = 632), participants interpreted AI uncertainty statements. The word used to describe the uncertainty (confidence, certainty, reliability, or accuracy) varied between trials. Participants often treated confidence and certainty as indicators of how sure the agent was about its output, whereas interpretations of reliability and accuracy were more variable. These findings can guide how AI systems communicate uncertainty, supporting more accurate user interpretations and robust decision-making.

items.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
items.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) remains a widely used approach for post-training large language models, because fixed demonstrations can directly introduce desired reasoning strategies and behavioral patterns. Yet forcing a model to imitate externally provided trajectories may also interfere with behaviors already supported by pretraining, limiting generalization beyond the training distribution. Recent dynamic SFT methods mitigate this issue by reweighting token-level supervision according to model-side signals such as predictive probability, prior support, or distributional compatibility. However, model compatibility is not equivalent to learning value: a token that is weakly supported by the current model may either be an undesirable mismatch or precisely the task-specific decision that the demonstration is intended to teach. We propose CIG-SFT, an information-theoretic framework that estimates the task-conditioned information carried by each demonstrated token. Under teacher forcing, we compare the token likelihood from a frozen reference model with and without access to the task input while keeping the gold solution prefix fixed. The resulting conditional information gain quantifies how much the task itself reduces uncertainty about the demonstrated decision. We then convert this information into a KL-regularized projection of the current policy and derive an equivalent scalar-weighted SFT objective whose logit gradient exactly matches that of the projected target. Across mathematical reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, CIG-SFT consistently outperforms standard SFT and recent adaptive fine-tuning baselines, with particularly strong improvements in generalization to challenging evaluation distributions, while requiring neither additional training data nor online rollouts.

items.title: When MLLMs miss what humans read: diagnosing and learning to read squint text
items.abstract: Multimodal LLMs can fail to read text embedded in an image's coarse structure (text a human recovers by squinting) and report that no text is present. We name this class Squint Text and study it as a recognition deficiency, motivated by cases from a production moderation pipeline. We introduce SquintBench, comprising 1076 production-derived moderation images, and SquintCtrl, a controlled synthetic suite for mechanism diagnosis. Frozen-weight analysis shows that hidden text leaves a coarse signal while glyph identity is weakly represented; identity becomes substantially more accessible when the correct spatial regions are supplied, implicating spatial selection as a major bottleneck. Suppressing high-frequency content also improves reading at a fixed visual-token budget, while visual token count may also contribute. These findings motivate Squint OPSD: a frozen teacher receives a downscaled view and the ground-truth transcription as privileged context, and its token-level distributions supervise a student along on-policy trajectories. At inference, the student reads the original image alone. Squint OPSD reaches 88.61 ANLS on SquintBench, versus 26.50 for the unadapted backbone, 24.44 for the best general-purpose model on the original view, and 68.60 at best for an off-the-shelf model under a downscaled view. These results substantially narrow the gap between available visual evidence and its generated read-out without auxiliary views at inference.

items.title: When One Size Doesn’t Fit All: Efficacy Assessment of an Engineering Control for Endoscopic Procedures
items.abstract: Studies report an elevated prevalence of endoscopy-related musculoskeletal disorders in gastroenterologists. Interventions primarily address work environment and work organization, not tool design (the endoscope). This study evaluated an add-on adjustable support strap designed to reduce the workload of the user’s left hand, which operates the endoscope’s control section. Study participants (four women, seven men) were experienced in endoscopy. Each participant performed two simulated colonoscopies with the support strap and two without (within-subjects design). Effects of the support strap were assessed using normalized muscle activity (nEMG) from surface electrodes over finger and wrist flexors and extensors and trapezius m., video, and usability data. With the strap, nEMG was reduced in most muscles for three participants (all women); mixed results for four, and no reduced nEMG for four others (all men). Mode of ratings of usability, usefulness, and desirability were 7, 5, 5, respectively (7 = very good). Results suggest benefits for some users.
